questions.question: State any two ways of identifying market opportunities. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• State any two ways of identifying market opportunities.
  • Conduct market research, surveys and consumer interviews to identify unmet needs.
  • Analyse market trends, competitors and gaps in existing products.

questions.question: Mention any two characteristics of a successful new food product. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention any two characteristics of a successful new food product.
  • It meets consumer needs and has acceptable taste, quality and convenience.
  • It is safe, affordable, commercially viable and differentiated from competing products.

questions.question: Explain the importance of licensing in international trade. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of licensing in international trade.
  • Licensing permits a company to use another firm's brand, technology, formula or process under
  • agreed terms.
  • It supports entry into foreign markets and defines usage rights, quality requirements and royalty
  • payments.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of packaging in maintaining product stability. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of packaging in maintaining product stability.
  • Packaging protects food from moisture, oxygen, light, contamination and physical damage.
  • Suitable packaging helps preserve quality and extend shelf life.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of comparing market samples in food quality evaluation. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of comparing market samples in food quality evaluation.
  • Comparison assesses colour, flavour, texture, appearance and acceptability against competing
  • products.
  • It identifies quality gaps and opportunities for improvement.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Why should food companies consider market competition while developing new products? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Why should food companies consider market competition while developing new products?
  • Competitor analysis reveals existing product features, prices, strengths and market gaps.
  • It helps companies differentiate the product and plan suitable positioning and pricing.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the role of market demand in food product development. / [CO1] [2x5 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• State the role of market demand in food product development.
  • Market demand indicates whether consumers are likely to buy the proposed product.
  • It guides product features, production volume, pricing and launch decisions.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe how changing consumer preferences create opportunities for new food product development. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how changing consumer preferences create opportunities for new food product
  • development.
  • Changing preferences—such as demand for convenience, health, plant-based foods or sustainable
  • packaging—reveal new consumer needs.
  • Companies can respond with suitable formulations, flavours, portion sizes and packaging.
  • Consumer research and product trials help confirm whether the product meets these needs.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the role of market testing in reducing product launch risk. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of market testing in reducing product launch risk.
  • Market testing introduces a product or concept to a limited target market before a full launch.
  • Feedback on taste, price, packaging and purchase intention reveals problems that can be corrected
  • early.
  • Results help estimate demand and improve launch, distribution and promotional decisions.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of shelf-life evaluation of food products. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of shelf-life evaluation of food products.
  • Shelf-life evaluation determines how long a product remains safe and acceptable under stated
  • storage conditions.
  • It monitors sensory, chemical and microbiological quality changes over time.
  • Results guide date marking, packaging choice and storage instructions.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the main steps involved in process design. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the main steps involved in process design.
  • Define product specifications and select suitable ingredients, equipment and processing operations.
  • Establish process parameters such as time, temperature and mixing conditions.
  • Conduct trials, validate quality and safety, and standardise the process for scale-up.

questions.question: Explain the contribution of novel food ingredients and processing technologies to product development. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the contribution of novel food ingredients and processing technologies to product
  • development.
  • Novel ingredients can improve nutrition, functionality, texture or flavour, or meet specific consumer
  • needs.
  • Advanced processing technologies may improve safety, quality, convenience or shelf life.
  • Assess ingredients and technologies for safety, regulatory compliance, cost and consumer acceptance.

questions.question: Explain the relationship between product design and formulation in new food product development. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the relationship between product design and formulation in new food product
  • development.
  • Product design defines the concept, target consumer, sensory attributes, format and positioning.
  • Formulation specifies the ingredients and proportions needed to achieve the desired characteristics.
  • Trials align the formulation with product specifications, safety, cost and consumer expectations.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the major technological advances that support new food product development. / [CO1] [4x5 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the major technological advances that support new food product development.
  • Advanced processing methods, including high-pressure and other non-thermal approaches, can help
  • preserve quality while ensuring safety.
  • Ingredient technologies and encapsulation enable new textures, flavours and nutritional features.
  • Modern packaging, rapid testing and digital tools support quality control and shelf-life improvement.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of consumer trials, market testing and sensory, chemical and microbiological assessment in deciding whether a newly developed food product is ready for commercialization. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the role of consumer trials, market testing and sensory, chemical and microbiological
  • assessment in deciding whether a newly developed food product is ready for commercialization.
  • Consumer trials and market testing assess liking, purchase intention, acceptable price, packaging and
  • likely demand. Feedback identifies improvements and helps estimate commercial potential.
  • Sensory and chemical assessment: sensory tests evaluate appearance, aroma, taste and texture.
  • Chemical tests assess relevant composition and quality indicators such as pH, moisture or oxidation.
  • Microbiological assessment verifies safety and stability during the intended shelf life.
  • Commercialization should proceed only when safety and quality requirements are met, consumers
  • accept the product, and market and financial potential are reasonable.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Analyse the complete new food product development process from idea generation to commercialization. Explain the purpose of each stage and show how decisions at one stage influence the next stage. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the complete new food product development process from idea generation to
  • commercialization. Explain the purpose of each stage and show how decisions at one stage
  • influence the next stage.
  • Idea generation and screening: Generate ideas from consumer needs, trends, research and
  • competitors; screen out unsuitable, unsafe or commercially unrealistic ideas.
  • Concept development and feasibility: Define the target market and product benefits; assess technical
  • feasibility, ingredient availability, cost, regulations and market potential. These findings determine
  • whether development should continue.
  • Formulation, process design and prototype testing: Select ingredients and processing conditions,
  • prepare prototypes, and evaluate sensory, chemical and microbiological quality. Results guide
  • reformulation and process changes.
  • Consumer and market testing: Obtain feedback on acceptability, price, packaging and purchase
  • intention. Use results to refine the product and marketing plan.
  • Scale-up and commercialization: Standardise the process, verify safety and quality, finalise
  • packaging and labelling, arrange production and distribution, and launch. Post-launch feedback
  • informs future improvements.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the changes in marketing strategies, sales and profit from the introduction stage to the decline stage of a new food product. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the changes in marketing strategies, sales and profit from the introduction stage to the
  • decline stage of a new food product.
  • Introduction: Sales are usually low while awareness and distribution are built. Promotion and launch
  • costs are high, so profit may be low or negative. Marketing focuses on informing consumers and
  • encouraging trial.
  • Growth and maturity: Sales rise as acceptance and distribution increase. Profit improves, but
  • competition intensifies. Marketing emphasises differentiation, brand loyalty, competitive pricing and
  • product variants.
  • Decline: Sales and profits fall because of changing preferences, alternatives or market saturation. A
  • company may reduce costs, reposition or modify the product, target a smaller segment, or discontinue it.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of integrating market analysis and sensory analysis in food product development. / [CO5] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of integrating market analysis and sensory analysis in food product
  • development.
  • Market analysis identifies target consumers, needs, trends, competitors, price expectations and
  • potential demand.
  • Sensory analysis measures product attributes such as taste, aroma, appearance and texture through
  • structured testing and consumer preference studies.
  • Integration ensures that the product is both acceptable to consumers and competitive. Market
  • findings guide sensory targets, while sensory results help refine formulation and support positioning,
  • pricing and launch decisions.
